user:
QUESTION: In the standard argument that PA does not derive its own consistency statement $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}}$, one uses the Gödel sentence $G_{\mathrm{PA}}$ for PA. What implication linking $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}}$ and $G_{\mathrm{PA}}$ is shown to be derivable in PA, and what tools are used to establish it?

ATOM: Letting $G_{\mathrm{PA}}$ be the Gödel sentence for PA, the derivability conditions (P1)–(P3) are used to show that PA derives $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}} \to G_{\mathrm{PA}}$, which is used to show that PA does not derive $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}}$.
KEY POINTS:
1. PA derives $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}} \to G_{\mathrm{PA}}$
2. It is established using the derivability conditions (P1)–(P3)

ANSWER TO GRADE:
The implication provable in PA is $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}} \to G_{\mathrm{PA}}$ (equivalently, PA proves that if PA is consistent then the Gödel sentence holds). It is established inside PA using the formalized provability predicate $\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}$ with the Hilbert–Bernays–Löb derivability conditions (including formalized completeness/soundness-style reasoning, i.e., that PA proves $G_{\mathrm{PA}} \leftrightarrow \neg\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner G_{\mathrm{PA}}\urcorner)$ and that $\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner G\urcorner)\to \mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner \mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner G\urcorner)\urcorner)$ type reasoning, so that $\mathrm{Con}_{\mathrm{PA}}$, read as $\neg\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner 0=1\urcorner)$, implies $\neg\mathrm{Prov}_{\mathrm{PA}}(\ulcorner G_{\mathrm{PA}}\urcorner)$, hence $G_{\mathrm{PA}}$).
